source.title: In Search of Grandmother Cells: Tracing Interpretable Neurons in Tabular Representations

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses superposition as background but does not test overlapping feature directions, capacity competition, SAE features, or feature dimensionality. Its experiments measure neuron–concept selectivity in TabPFN.
record.gate_note: The reported neuron–concept selectivity results are recorded as findings about the claim's subject, but they do not test any listed version: the study does not measure superposition geometry, capacity competition, causes of polysemanticity, LLM feature distributions, SAE feature completeness, or feature dimensionality. TabPFN AUC and the sparse-probe comparisons do not test those claims and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The paper mentions superposition only as background in Related Work. Its experiments measure the single-neuron surprisal and selectivity of TabPFN neurons for ICD concepts. It does not measure feature geometry, capacity competition, causes of polysemanticity, SAE features, or feature dimensionality. It finds no 'grandmother cells' (selectivity ≤0.73). That is consistent with neurons responding to more than one concept, but the study never tests superposition or its causes. TabPFN is also not an LLM, so V4 does not apply.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is correct. The authors report moderate, statistically significant saliency and selectivity for some high-level concepts in TabPFN on 2 of 4 tasks, with no grandmother cells (selectivity ≤0.73). They present their information-theoretic framework as a simple tool that does not need SAEs or probes.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses information-theoretic neuron–concept metrics and a Pareto-front search on TabPFN representations, rather than the original toy-model superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The significance outcome varies by prediction task: two tasks have p < 0.05 and two have p ≥ 0.05.

fits_no_version.finding: In TabPFN, most neurons are neither salient nor selective for ICD concepts. The best knee-point neurons reach selectivity of 0.30–0.73, which is statistically significant in 2 of 4 tasks. No neuron responds near-exclusively to a single concept.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single neurons in a tabular foundation model show at most moderate selectivity for high-level clinical concepts (≤0.73); no near-monosemantic 'grandmother cells' are found.

record.peer_reviewed: EurIPS 2025 Workshop on AI for Tabular Data
record.problems: The authors note that the significance tests are asymptotic and assume i.i.d. scores, without accounting for data scarcity or structural dependencies in the network or concept hierarchy. They also report that significance is not reached in all tasks and that selectivity does not exceed 0.73.

untested.parts: Toy networks, the ratio of sparse features to dimensions, nearly orthogonal overlapping directions, the sparsity transition, and geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity, and whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Distributed features in LLMs and SAE recovery of sparse features. No SAE is trained, and TabPFN is not an LLM.
Completeness, stability, and canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: The sparse-probe baselines being Pareto-dominated is a comparison of the study's own method and is rightly omitted. Selectivity depends on the size of the concept set (high-level codes, C=24), so the absolute values are not comparable across studies.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse feature counts relative to dimensions, overlapping or nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity, and whether feature importance determines which features get dedicated dimensions versus sharing.
Whether polysemanticity arises through other mechanisms or is insufficient evidence for superposition.
LLM feature distribution across neurons and sparse features recoverable by a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.
